short: The last emperor to rule a united Roman Empire, which split permanently between his two sons on his death.
full:
Theodosius, a Spanish-born general, was raised to emperor of the east on 19 January 379 CE to stabilise the frontier after the Gothic victory at Adrianople three years earlier, negotiating a settlement that allowed the Goths to settle within imperial territory as an autonomous ally. He became sole ruler of the whole empire in 392 CE after defeating two western usurpers, the second time he had marched west to reimpose unity by force.

Theodosius died at Milan on 17 January 395 CE, dividing the empire between his sons Arcadius in the east and Honorius in the west. Unlike earlier divisions among co-emperors, this one was never reunited: the eastern and western courts drifted permanently apart, and no single ruler again governed the whole Roman world.
